name: yourstopwashit-mcp

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: The YourStopWasHit plans with their current prices and features, read live from the site. Use it to tell a user what a gated tool costs.

tools.name: get_signals
tools.description: Fetch generated options-flow research signals from the last N days, newest first. Set sweepOnly=true to return only signals where sweep activity was one of the confirming components. Set scored=true to return only signals that already have graded outcomes. By default the answer holds the newest 20 signals with their key fields (time, direction, vehicle, confirming symbols, active components, levels, outcome, exit and graded P&L percent) and count covers all of them; limit returns more rows and verbose=true adds the per-component detail, feature, GEX and regime blocks (a week of full rows can exceed 250 KB). Needs an account token (any plan).

days.description: Number of days of history to include (1-30, default 7).

sweepOnly.description: If true, return only sweep-confirmed signals.

scored.description: If true, return only signals that have recorded outcomes.

verbose.description: If true, return every field (and, without limit, every row): the full answer, which can be large.

tools.name: get_public_signals
tools.description: Fetch the public derived signals feed: per signal its time, direction, vehicle, confirming symbols, active components and outcome (no raw prints; the engine's conviction score is not included). Newest first over the last 7 days unless you sort or filter. With neither page nor limit the answer holds the newest 20 signals and says how to get more; with page and no limit a page is 50 signals.

limit.description: Signals per page (1-200; default 20 on a first call, 50 when page is given).

ticker.description: Restrict to one underlying symbol, e.g. SPY.

days.description: Days of history to read (1-30, default 7).

tools.name: get_signals_today
tools.description: Fetch the signals generated during the current trading day, newest first, including conviction and timestamps. Use this for an intraday snapshot of what the flow engine has fired so far today. By default the newest 20 signals with their key fields (count covers all of them); limit returns more rows and verbose=true every field. Needs an account token (any plan).

verbose.description: If true, return every field (and, without limit, every row): the full answer, which can be large.

tools.name: get_top_signals
tools.description: Fetch the published research signals of the last 24 hours that are still open (unresolved), newest first. It is a list, not a ranking: the API does not publish, rank, filter or sort by the conviction score, which the site's own research has not found predictive (see get_signal_accuracy). Entry, target and stop of an open signal need a free account token (any plan); without one the list carries symbol, direction and time, and the levels become public on the receipt (get_receipt) when the signal resolves. Filter by symbol or direction. minConviction and minSampleN are retired and ignored by the API.

limit.description: Max number of signals to return (1-50, default 5).

minConviction.description: Retired. Accepted for compatibility and ignored by the API.

minSampleN.description: Retired. Accepted for compatibility and ignored by the API.

symbol.description: Restrict to a single underlying symbol, e.g. SPY.

tools.name: get_track_record
tools.description: Fetch the public signal performance history (win rate, wins/losses, average return, best signal) over the last N days. The win rate uses the site's canonical record: expired signals are reported separately and drift-graded rows are excluded, so the decided sample can be much smaller than the signal count. Always quote sampleSize (and insufficientData when true) with the rate. get_track_record_rows has the rows behind these counts.

days.description: Number of days of history to include (1-90, default 30).

tools.name: get_signal_accuracy
tools.description: Fetch overall signal accuracy metrics: total scored, correct count, pending count, window in days, and a per-type accuracy breakdown. Use this to judge how reliable the signal engine has been.

tools.name: get_signals_context
tools.description: Fetch a natural-language + structured summary of the recent signal track record (totals, resolved, wins/losses, win rate, current streak) over the last N days. Good as a compact narrative primer before reasoning about signals. Needs an account token (any plan).

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: Fetch the public product/statistics summary: trades tracked, signals generated, total notional, signal hit rate, and last-updated timestamp. The hit rate comes without its sample size: for the sample size and exclusions call get_track_record, and do not quote this rate alone.

tools.name: get_market_pulse
tools.description: Fetch a one-call market overview: overall market bias, sentiment, market status (open/closed), data freshness, and the top symbols by flow. The best single starting call for broad market context.

tools.name: get_market_brief
tools.description: Fetch the macro-flavored market brief: session, fear score, VIX spot and VX term-structure. Complements market-pulse with volatility/risk framing.

window.description: Flow lookback window in minutes (5-240, default 30).

tools.name: get_flow_bias
tools.description: Fetch the current market bias derived from options flow: overall marketBias, the window in minutes, data freshness, and a per-symbol bias/score breakdown (call vs put notional).

tools.name: get_daily_briefing
tools.description: Fetch the daily options-flow briefing: dominant side, put/call ratio, tilt-flip count, morning-thesis narrative, and VIX context. Pass a date (YYYY-MM-DD) to retrieve a historical briefing, or window to change the flow lookback window.

window.description: Flow lookback window in minutes (5-240, default 30).

date.description: Historical date in YYYY-MM-DD (CST). Omit for today's live briefing.

tools.name: get_commentary
tools.description: Fetch a short natural-language commentary summarizing the current market bias and the largest flow of the day. Useful as a human-readable one-liner of context.

tools.name: get_anomalies
tools.description: Fetch recent options-flow anomalies as plain-English event descriptions (large prints, sentiment/tilt flips, etc.), newest first.

limit.description: Max number of anomalies to return (1-50, default 20).

tools.name: get_0dte_summary
tools.description: Fetch a summary of same-day-expiry (0DTE) options flow: total notional, call vs put percentage, and the top symbols with prints.

tools.name: get_market_regime
tools.description: One-call read of current market conditions: trend, dealer gamma sign, volatility state (from the VIX percentile) and whether today has a high-importance macro event, each with its source and as-of time; how many of five independent directional reads agree and which way; the day's largest unexpired $1M+ options print described in plain words; how many signals the quality gates generated, filtered and published today; VIX spot and change; and a list of every input that is missing right now. agreement.total counts only the reads that were available (it can be 1 of 5), so always quote agree together with total. The largest print is a description of one third-party trade; the site's own study grades single large prints near 50% for direction (see get_print_attribution). Use it as a first call for market state. It reports conditions only.

tools.name: get_flow_tilt
tools.description: Premium-weighted tilt of options flow for the last 30 minutes and for the session so far: overall side, the index reading with bull and bear premium, per-sector readings, breadth (share of sectors leaning each way), whether sectors agree with the index, a confidence value, a thin flag when there are too few prints, and momentum against the session (accelerating, fading, flipping, steady, or unknown whenever either window is thin), plus the method note. Use it to check whether index flow is confirmed by sector flow. Empty and thin outside market hours.

tools.name: get_flow_players
tools.description: Per-symbol totals of today's options tape since the 08:30 CT open: the 15 symbols with the most premium, each with print count, put dollars, call dollars, put share, sweep count and its single largest print (type, strike, expiry, notional, time). Totals cover the prints currently held in memory for the window named in `window`; after a service restart or on very busy symbols they can undercount the session. After 15:00 CT and outside the session the window is the last 60 minutes. Includes the site's note that the direction of flow alone has graded at about 50% in its own research. Use it to see which names have an active tape today. Empty outside market hours.

tools.name: get_morning_tape
tools.description: The opening options-tape read (research registry R-025): the put share of SPY and QQQ options premium between 08:30 and 08:50 CT, frozen after 08:50. Without a paid plan: state (closed, pre_open, measuring, frozen), the band (put_heavy, mixed, call_heavy), a one-sentence description and day context (weekday, FOMC today or yesterday, options expiration, month edge). With a Pro token: the exact share, print counts, per-symbol split, VIX context and the in-sample table per band (54 days, in-sample, not a forecast). A null band with state frozen means the opening window's prints are not available (holiday or service restart), not a neutral tape. Use it for how the session opened.

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: The symbols the site ingests options flow for right now: the effective equity and ETF list (about 50) and the futures roots, with an as-of time. Use it before per-symbol flow tools to check that a symbol is covered; symbols outside the list return empty results.

tools.name: get_symbol_context
tools.description: Fetch a context score for a specific symbol and direction: an aggregate of background factors (dealer gamma regime, Fed stance, bitcoin tone and insider activity) with a list of contributors. It scores the backdrop for that direction; it is not a rating of the symbol.

direction.description: Direction to score context for (default bullish).

tools.name: get_gex
tools.description: Fetch dealer gamma-exposure (GEX) data. Omit symbol for the multi-symbol snapshot; pass a symbol (tracked: SPY, QQQ, IWM) for that ticker's gamma profile. Note: a symbol with no current snapshot returns a 404 with the tracked list.

symbol.description: Optional symbol (SPY, QQQ, or IWM). Omit for all tracked symbols.

tools.name: get_next_candles
tools.description: Fetch the output of the site's next-candle model for a symbol: the recent actual candles and the model's next candles. Omit symbol to get the supported-symbol / interval metadata. Through this server only SPY at the 1m interval is available: every other symbol/interval combination answers 402 for all account tokens today. Answers 503 when no model output is available, which is usual outside market hours. The model has no published graded record (get_forecast_accuracy grades a different forecast), so treat the output as an unverified model path, not as a forecast.

symbol.description: Symbol (SPY, QQQ, IWM, ES, NQ, NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, META, AMZN, GOOG, MSFT). Omit for metadata.

tools.name: get_flow_summary
tools.description: Fetch the stored end-of-day summary of the options tape for one session: date, a written summary, bias score and direction, call, put and total premium, total prints, call/put ratio, the largest print, signals generated and the top symbols by premium. Omit date for the most recent stored session; pass date (YYYY-MM-DD) for an earlier one. A 404 means no summary is stored for that date. Without a paid plan the body carries the site's free-access label (delayed:true, delayMinutes:15); a stored summary of a finished session is complete either way.

date.description: Session date, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the most recent stored session.

tools.name: get_flow_unusual_activity
tools.description: Fetch symbols showing unusual options activity right now — volume spikes vs a rolling baseline, with direction. Highlights where flow is concentrating. Needs an account token (any plan).

tools.name: get_flow_iv_rank
tools.description: Fetch implied-volatility rank per symbol (current IV vs its recent lookback range). Use to spot rich vs cheap volatility across the tracked universe. Needs an account token on the Pro plan.

window.description: Window for the current IV in minutes (5-120, default 30).

lookback.description: History to rank against in minutes (60-43200, default 43200 = 30 days).

tools.name: get_flow_market_intel
tools.description: Fetch intraday market-intel derived from the flow tape: a time heatmap of notional and count by minute, sweep percentages, and related aggregates. Needs an account token (any plan).

tools.name: get_darkpool_activity
tools.description: Fetch recent detected dark-pool print activity (count, data freshness, and the activity list). Complements lit options flow with off-exchange block context. Needs an account token (any plan).

tools.name: get_levels_map
tools.description: Structural levels for one index ETF (SPY, QQQ or IWM) in one call: last price and session open, expected move from at-the-money implied volatility, and gamma exposure (net GEX, zero-gamma flip, long or short gamma regime, the three largest call walls and put walls). spot has no timestamp of its own and the top-level asOf is the response time; outside the regular session spot is the last trade seen and the em and gex as-of times are cache-refresh times. gex.flip can be null while regime is set. Use it for a levels picture of one index; get_gex has the full per-strike profile.

symbol.description: Index ETF: SPY, QQQ or IWM.

tools.name: get_dealer_map
tools.description: Dealer gamma positioning for SPY and QQQ from the site's own option-chain snapshots (research registry R-035, not yet measured against outcomes). Without a paid plan: the gamma regime (positive or negative), the snapshot time (snapshot_ts), a stale flag and one plain sentence per symbol. With a Pro token: regime strength, zero-gamma flip, call and put walls, total GEX, a plus or minus 3% strike ladder, the 0DTE-only read and contract counts. It describes where dealers are positioned and how they hedge, not where price goes.

symbol.description: SPY or QQQ. Omit for both.

tools.name: get_contract_facts
tools.description: Measured facts about one option contract that the caller specifies: days to expiry, cost of one contract at the given premium (assumes the standard 100 multiplier of equity and ETF options), live bid-ask spread in percent with its timestamp, underlying price, the percent move needed to break even at expiry, the expected move to expiry from at-the-money implied volatility, the ratio of breakeven to expected move, and a note on time decay. It is arithmetic on the inputs you supply plus live quotes; it does not select, grade or rank contracts. thetaNote is fixed site copy keyed on days to expiry only, the same for every contract with that many days. Each fact is null when its live source is stale, which is common outside market hours. found:false means the contract details could not be parsed. Expired contracts are refused.

symbol.description: Equity or ETF symbol, e.g. SPY, NVDA, BRK.B. Futures roots are not supported.

expiry.description: Expiry date, YYYY-MM-DD. Today or later (America/Chicago).

optPrice.description: Premium per share. Without it contractCost, breakevenPct and beOverEm are null.

tools.name: get_0dte_contract_stories
tools.description: For one trading day, the five same-day-expiry option contracts (from 15 liquid symbols) whose price rose the most between their first and highest print: contract, first, peak and last print price and time, the peak multiple and the end-of-day multiple, print count, total notional, the largest print, and the underlying price at the first and last print. Always comes with the six-month census (share of contract-days that touched 2x versus the share that still held 2x, 5x and 10x at the last print) and the site's note that the peak multiple is hindsight: it assumes buying the first print and selling the exact high. truncated:true means the day's read was capped and the ranking is partial; for today the list changes until the close. Use it to study how 0DTE contracts moved on a recent day, with the census as the base rate. Empty for days without a session.

date.description: Day to read, YYYY-MM-DD: today or one of the previous 10 calendar days. Default: today (America/Chicago).

tools.name: get_flow_timeline
tools.description: Options flow over time: for each time bucket the call, put, buy-side, sell-side and same-day-expiry premium (callNot, putNot, buyNot, sellNot, d0Not), print count, total notional and call/put ratio, for one symbol or the whole tape. Use it to see how flow built up during the session. Needs an account token (any plan); each call counts against the free plan's daily call limit. On the free plan the newest 15 minutes are withheld and the body says delayed:true. Built from the live session, so it is empty outside market hours.

symbol.description: Underlying symbol, e.g. SPY. Omit for the whole tape.

tools.name: get_macro_events
tools.description: Fetch recent macro events (Fed statements, minutes, speeches, testimony, press releases) with source, title, url, summary, and a hawkish/dovish/neutral stance.

tools.name: get_macro_indicators
tools.description: Fetch a set of macro indicator series (e.g. the 10Y-2Y yield-curve spread) with their latest values and as-of dates.

tools.name: get_macro_calendar
tools.description: Fetch upcoming scheduled macro events (FOMC meetings, key data releases) with type, title, and timing.

from.description: Optional start date/time filter (ISO or YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: get_earnings_calendar
tools.description: Upcoming earnings reports for today plus the next 7 days, from the NASDAQ public calendar: symbol, company name, report date and timing (BMO = before the open, AMC = after the close, or UNKNOWN), with a count. A count of 0 means the calendar could not be loaded, not that nobody reports. Use it to see which companies report soon.

tools.name: get_sec_filings
tools.description: Fetch the most recent SEC filings (form type, company, ticker, filer, filed-at, url, and any transaction detail). Filter by form type, e.g. 4 for insider forms.

form.description: Filter by SEC form type, e.g. '4', '8-K', '13F'.

tools.name: get_sec_insider_buys
tools.description: Fetch recent insider BUY transactions parsed from SEC Form 4 filings, optionally filtered to a minimum transaction value.

limit.description: Max insider buys to return (1-100, default 20).

tools.name: get_news
tools.description: Fetch the recent market news feed (titles and metadata) used for signal-relevant context and news flags. For one ticker use get_symbol_news.

tools.name: get_symbol_news
tools.description: Recent third-party news articles for one ticker ranked by relevance: title, publisher, publish time, link, tickers, a short summary, the provider's per-ticker sentiment label, and sentiment and relevance scores. Use it for headlines on a single name. An empty list can also mean the news provider failed; retry once. Opinions in the articles belong to their publishers.

symbol.description: Ticker, 1-5 letters, e.g. NVDA. Symbols with dots are not supported.

tools.name: get_news_digest
tools.description: Market news digest: about 20 current headlines (title, publisher, link, tickers), the site's overall options-flow bias with the symbols leaning most bullish and most bearish, and key events; marked stale outside market hours. flowBias NEUTRAL with empty lists means no flow snapshot was available. Use it for a quick news scan; get_symbol_news covers one ticker. Headlines are the publishers' own words, shown with source and link; they are not the site's views.

tools.name: get_retail_sentiment
tools.description: Fetch retail social sentiment: the most-mentioned tickers and post/source counts aggregated from retail chatter.

tools.name: get_crypto
tools.description: Fetch crypto price data. Omit ticker for the tracked-coin list (BTC, ETH, ...) with 24h change; pass a ticker (e.g. BTC) for that single coin.

ticker.description: Optional coin ticker, e.g. BTC, ETH. Omit for all tracked coins.

tools.name: get_research_registry
tools.description: The site's research registry: every hypothesis it has tested (R-001 onward) with the verdict in the title, including the rejected and unproven ones. Without a paid plan: all entry ids and titles plus the full text of the first two entries. With a Pro token: by default the protocol preamble, every entry id and title (the verdict is in the title) and the sections after the entries (the open research queue); pass id (e.g. R-020) for one entry's full text, or verbose=true for the whole registry in Markdown (about 50 KB). asOf is the time of the response, not the time the registry last changed. Use it to see what the site's research has and has not been able to show, including every rejected idea.

id.description: One entry id, e.g. R-020: returns that entry's full text.

verbose.description: If true, return every field (and, without limit, every row): the full answer, which can be large.

tools.name: get_print_attribution
tools.description: Out-of-sample study of what the underlying did after large option prints, split into four groups (bought calls, sold calls, bought puts, sold puts): sample sizes for the fit and out-of-sample windows, baseline-adjusted forward moves in basis points at 30 minutes, 1 hour and the close, out-of-sample hit rates, totals and the two date windows. Refreshed nightly; returns available:false while the nightly cache is empty. Use it for the measured answer to whether a large print predicts direction; quote hitOos together with nOos.

tools.name: get_track_record_rows
tools.description: Row-level ledger behind the published signal track record: each resolved published signal with id, time, symbol, direction, entry, target and stop on the underlying, horizon in minutes, resolution price and source, outcome (win, loss or expired), resolution time and a receipt path, plus window counts of wins, losses and expired, a truncated flag and the grading methodology. counts and total describe the whole window; rows holds only the newest `limit` of them (compare rows.length with total). truncated:true means the ledger read itself was capped. Expired signals are reported separately, never counted as wins or losses, and have no resolution price. Use it to audit get_track_record or to find signal ids for get_receipt. These are historical results of published research signals and do not predict future ones.

tools.name: get_receipt
tools.description: Resolve a citation key to the archived record it refers to. A signal key returns the published signal's time, symbol, direction, entry, target, stop, outcome, exit price and time, and the percent move of the underlying. A print key returns the archived options print: time, symbol, type, strike, expiry, price, size, notional, side and sweep flag. The answer includes verified, mismatches and the grading methodology. For a print key, verified and mismatches compare the symbol, strike and expiry inside the key with the archived print; for a signal key verified is always true and only means the record exists and is published. Use it to verify one specific claim. Unknown, unpublished or quarantined records return 404.

key.description: Either a signal id 'sig-...' (case-sensitive, from get_track_record_rows) or 'print:{printId}:{symbol}:{strike}:{expiry}' as printed on the site's content cards.

tools.name: get_forecast_accuracy
tools.description: Graded record of the site's daily AI close forecast: per symbol the number of resolved forecasts, mean absolute error of the forecast close against the actual close in percent, and directional hit rate, also split by the forecast's stated confidence, plus total_resolved for the lookback. It does NOT grade get_next_candles, which is a separate model with no published record. The sample is small; always quote the counts with any rate. A graded record, not a claim of skill.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description: Fetch the signal leaderboard for a period (today, week, or month): the ten published signals with the largest theoretical move of the underlying after the signal. It is a hindsight selection of the largest moves with no sample size, not the record: get_track_record has the full record with wins, losses and sample size.

tools.name: get_antonio_trades
tools.description: Fetch the trade log of Antonio, the site's paper-trading robot (simulated money in a TastyTrade sandbox account, no real money): symbol, direction, entry, conviction, outcome. Filter to the last week or month. Paper results do not predict future ones. The log is newest first. By default only the newest 20 trades of the period are returned, with a one-line note saying how many more there are; limit keeps the newest N instead and verbose=true returns the whole period (period=all is large: about 400 trades, roughly 170 KB; period=week is small, a few KB).

period.description: Time window: all, week, or month (default all).

limit.description: Keep only the newest N trades of the period (1-500, default 20).

verbose.description: If true and limit is omitted, return the whole period (can be about 170 KB).

tools.name: get_antonio_stats
tools.description: Fetch aggregate stats for Antonio, the site's paper-trading robot (simulated money in a TastyTrade sandbox account, no real money): win rate, total paper P&L, total trades, average conviction, and direction accuracy. Quote the trade count with any rate.

tools.name: get_antonio_account
tools.description: Fetch the state of Antonio's paper account (a TastyTrade sandbox, simulated money, no real money): net-liq, cash, open-position count, realized paper P&L, starting capital, and a net-liq history for the equity curve.

tools.name: get_arena_summary
tools.description: State of the Arena, the site's competition between paper-trading robots (simulated trades, no real money): whether the market is open and when it next opens, how many robots are active, still measuring (under 30 settled trades) or ranked, today's counts of trades, entries, skips, settled and open positions, time since the last trade, the current leader's id and name, and the sample-size floors used for rates and ranks. The measuring count is every robot that is not ranked, including those the board labels open. With a Pro token it adds the settled paper results of the leader, best and worst robots and short generated observations. Use it as the first Arena call.

tools.name: get_arena_leaders
tools.description: Top 10 and bottom 10 Arena paper-trading robots for a period, and results pooled by research family, with the period's date range and session count (range): on a weekend or before the open, today means the last session, and range says which. Without a paid plan each row has the robot's id, name, family, whether it was up, down or flat, and its settled-trade count n. With a Pro token rows add paper P&L, wins and win percentage. All results are simulated paper trades; quote n with any rate and treat robots under 30 settled trades as still measuring. Use it for who is ahead or behind in a period; the ids work with get_arena_bot.

period.description: today, week, month or all (default week).

tools.name: get_arena_board
tools.description: Full roster of Arena paper-trading robots (about 135): id, name, research family, house or user-published, one-line thesis, status (ranked, measuring under the 30-trade floor, open, or an error state) and schedule. With a Pro token each robot also carries its rank, settled n, effective n, win percentage, expectancy, lower confidence bound, total paper P&L and last trade date; control clones share an identical ledger with another robot (clone_of) and carry no rank. Settled statistics only: open positions and individual trades are not returned. By default the answer holds the first 20 robots in board order (ranked robots by lower confidence bound, then the rest by settled n) without thesis and schedule, and says how many more match; limit returns more rows and verbose=true adds thesis and schedule (the whole roster with every field is about 80 KB). Optional family and status filters shrink the list; the answer lists the family names. Simulated paper trading only. The call can take up to 10 seconds.

family.description: Keep only one research family, e.g. volatility (names are listed in the answer).

status.description: Keep only robots with this status.

limit.description: Robots to return, in board order (1-200, default 20).

verbose.description: If true, return every field (and, without limit, every row): the full answer, which can be large.

tools.name: get_arena_bot
tools.description: One Arena paper-trading robot by id: name, research family, house or user-published, thesis, status and a count of its most recent ledger rows (at most 60, so not its lifetime total). With a Pro token it adds the robot's settled statistics: n, effective n, win percentage, expectancy, lower confidence bound, paper P&L and maximum drawdown (rank is reported by get_arena_board and can be null here). Individual trades are not returned. Simulated paper trading only; under 30 settled trades the robot is still measuring. Unknown or hidden robots return 404.

id.description: Robot id (UUID) from get_arena_board or get_arena_leaders.

tools.name: get_arena_gates
tools.description: The five pre-registered go/no-go gates for the site's own internal PAPER book (called The Fund on the site; it takes no outside money and is not an investment product): each gate's description, current status (pass, fail or measuring) and the evidence behind it (paper NAV of both tracks, robots at the 30-trade rank floor, broker-sandbox fills, circuit-breaker status, comparison with holding cash and with SPY), plus the window start and session count. The response labels itself paper: no real money is traded. Use it to see how the site holds its own paper results to account.

tools.name: get_arena_fund
tools.description: The site's own internal PAPER book (called The Fund on the site; it takes no outside money and is not an investment product): a paper rehearsal of a rule set applied to the top-ranked Arena robots. Without a paid plan: the rules (book size, per-trade risk cap, maximum deployment, daily loss breaker, rank floors, commissions, weekly review) and the number of days recorded. With a Pro token: daily paper NAV, P&L and deployed risk for the strict and rehearsal tracks, which robots are funded, and the days the breaker tripped. Individual trades are not returned. No real money is traded.

tools.name: get_arena_families
tools.description: Arena results pooled by research family: the question each family tests, its robots with settled n, effective n, expectancy and lower confidence bound, the pooled expectancy across the family, its control robots and their expectancy, and how many experiments have been measured and how many were above their control. Simulated paper trades; expectancy is withheld under 10 settled trades and the lower confidence bound is null below the 30-trade effective-n floor. By default each family lists its first 5 robots (controls first, then most settled trades) without thesis sentences, with bots_total per family; limit returns more robots per family and verbose=true every field (about 75 KB). Needs Pro; a free token gets counts only.

verbose.description: If true, return every field (and, without limit, every row): the full answer, which can be large.

tools.name: get_arena_lab
tools.description: Cross-robot condition study over the Arena's settled paper trades: the dimensions and filters examined, market conditions under which pooled results were above or below the rest with their thresholds and sample sizes, candidates with too little data, the measured effect of each filter, and open hypotheses. By default each list keeps its first 10 rows (conditions sorted by the size of the difference) with a short stat block per side, and totals gives every list's length; limit returns more rows per list and verbose=true every field (the full study can exceed 150 KB). Pooled, simulated, in-sample observations, not rules. Needs Pro; a free token gets counts only.

verbose.description: If true, return every field (and, without limit, every row): the full answer, which can be large.

tools.name: get_arena_features
tools.description: The market measurements the Arena robots read for SPY or QQQ: a flat map of about 100 named measurements of current market state (null = not available) covering flow, print side, price, volatility, context, greeks, published-signal counts, futures, market breadth and news, with the time computed (computed_at) and the list of feature names. Market context, not trades: what the robots themselves are doing is not included. Needs Pro; a free token gets the symbol and a feature count only.

tools.name: get_context_backtest
tools.description: Fetch a backtest of the context-score buckets vs realized signal outcomes over N days (wins/losses per alignment bucket). Shows whether higher context scores actually correlated with better outcomes. It counts a wider set of signals than the site's canonical record, so its win and loss totals do not match get_track_record: use get_track_record for the track record itself.

instructions: YourStopWasHit research data for AI agents: options-flow signals, market context and regime, per-symbol flow and levels, macro / SEC / news / earnings, the site's research registry and graded records, and the Arena, the public scoreboard of the site's paper-trading robots. Every tool is read-only: nothing here places an order or touches a brokerage account. The data is research and education, not investment advice, and past results of signals or paper trades do not predict future ones. Robot results are simulated paper trades: hypothetical results have inherent limitations and do not represent actual trading; always quote the sample size with any rate. Free data can be delayed about 15 minutes. Most tools work with no token; the rest need an account token (EDGE_TOKEN) and return what the owner's plan includes. Some tools return a free preview, marked as such, when the plan does not include the full body. List tools answer short by default (the first rows, key fields only); when anything was left out, one line above the answer says how many and how to get them (limit, or verbose=true). Call get_pricing for the current plans.
